target_customer: Students, with teachers as a secondary user; consumer subscription
problem: Students get stuck on math homework and want step by step help. Mathos (formerly MathGPTPro) offers photo based solving, tutoring hints and progress tracking, with grading tools for teachers.
business_model: Consumer subscription app and web, with teacher tools (pricing not verified)

founders.name: Tianwei Yue
founders.background_notes: YC page says he has worked in AI since 2015, including reinforcement learning and robotics, and language agents since 2022, mostly at tech companies. No schools or employers named.

technical_complexity.rationale: Photo to problem recognition and reliable multi step math reasoning on top of 2023 language models was hard to get accurate; the company claims 20 percent better accuracy than GPT-4o on its own tests, which is unverified.

defensibility.rationale: General chatbots and established solvers could solve the same problems, and student apps have low switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Comparison pages from 2025 and 2026 treat Photomath, Symbolab, Mathway and general chatbots as the alternatives; none acquired Mathos in the sources found.

market_need_then: Students searched for math help before generative AI, and 2023 chat models made step by step explanations cheap, though they also made frequent arithmetic errors, which created room for specialised tools.

branding.domain_note: Consumer web address was still mathgptpro.com as of a late 2024 blog post; the company site now uses mathos.ai.

identity.voice_and_tone: Optimistic, mission driven and encouraging, with lines such as No one is left behind.

rebrands.why: Not stated by a source; a December 2024 company blog post still uses both names

branding.community_and_virality: App store and review site listings exist; no independent press on the brand found.

brand_strength.rationale: The old name MathGPTPro was descriptive and confusable with other MathGPT tools, and the rename is only partly adopted, with some listings still using the old name.

outcome_analysis: Mathos is active with a team of about five and self reported user counts ranging from one million to five million students, which are unverified marketing claims. Public funding data is limited to aggregator listings of a small YC check, so the fundraising trajectory is unknown. It competes with free chatbots and established solvers.
notes: Funding unverified: aggregators list 500K USD from Y Combinator around April 2024, labelled pre-seed or convertible note. A Caplight page showing a 16M USD Series A belongs to another company and was ignored. Aggregators disagree on founders (one names Qi Lyu as CTO); only Tianwei Yue is on the YC page. Competitor search returned only 2025 and 2026 comparison pages, so none are recorded as of founding. The rename date is not sourced. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. Completeness pass: the 500K round around 2024-04 rests on databases only (CB Insights calls it a convertible note, VCBacked and FundedIQ a pre-seed); stage recorded as pre_seed from VCBacked and the instrument is unconfirmed.
